summary: Final invoice shows hosted charges not reflected in Console estimator after multi-model batch run
description: Issue summary: Customer ran a scheduled multi-model batch job (rerank + embedding pipeline) on 2026-03-08. Console estimator showed an expected hosted+dedicated blended estimate of ~$1,300 for the run; final invoice shows an additional $2,700 hosted charge. BrightLens claims they should have only consumed reserved dedicated capacity for the run, and that the Console estimator did not indicate potential hosted fallback costs. Impact: Unexpected $2,700 hosted charge on final invoice, customer requests explanation and credit if charge is not justified. Environment: Dedicated pool org-id=org-bltl, reserved-capacity plan (monthly commit), job submitted from orchestration service in us-east-1 at 2026-03-08T03:12:00Z. Attachments: customer-provided CSV of usage lines, sample batch job manifest, and Console estimator screenshot.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer scheduled batch job using pipeline: embedding -> rerank (multi-model) with concurrency 48 and retry_policy=standard. 2) Job began 2026-03-08T03:12:00Z and ran for ~3h. 3) During run, Console displayed sustained dedicated utilization ~98%, occasional autoscaler events. 4) Customer received final invoice on 2026-03-09 with hosted usage lines totaling $2,700 tagged as 'fallback-hosted' for same time window. 5) Customer cannot find corresponding requests in their reserved capacity audit logs; Console estimator had not warned of fallback risk.
logs: Customer-provided sample request IDs: req-20260308-3a7f, req-20260308-4b8c, req-20260308-9f1d. Billing lines (invoice #INV-2026-03-BL123): hosted usage lines 2026-03-08 03:40:12 - 06:51:22 tagged fallback-hosted total $2,700. Console dashboard screenshot: estimator predicted $1,300 (dedicated + hosted blended). Audit log snippet (customer): dedicated-pool-utilization.csv attached. Support pulled router logs: routing-service logged 'fallback route: hosted-variant' for batch bucket id batch-8818 at 2026-03-08T03:39:56Z (trace-id: trace-88aa).
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: requests spilled to hosted due to dedicated autoscaler cooldown or pool OOM/noisy-neighbor evictions. Support queried autoscaler events and found scale-down/start oscillation between 03:30-03:45 UTC; one scale-down attempted at 03:36 with pending scale-up requests queued. Router logs show host fallback for ~4,200 requests between 03:38-03:46. Billing pipeline attributes those requests to hosted product since they executed on hosted runtime. Console estimator logic: estimator uses historical run distribution to predict costs but does not currently model autoscaler cold-start/fallback probability. Confirmed linked internal ticket INT-4421: scheduler autoscaler flapping incident during same window. Related PR to adjust estimator already open but not merged (see related_github_prs).
comments: 2026-03-10 10:05 - Aisha Rahman (Support): Opened ticket after receiving customer's invoice CSV and estimator screenshot. Asked customer for job manifest and sample request IDs.

2026-03-11 14:20 - Elsa Martinez (Billing): Pulled invoice lines and router logs; confirmed hosted-tagged lines overlap job time window. Noted router logged fallback events. Escalated to SRE for autoscaler timeline.

2026-03-12 09:33 - SRE (Jon Park): Investigated autoscaler. Found a rapid scale-down at 03:36 caused by an aggressive cooldown misconfiguration on pool 'dedic-pool-bltl-1' combined with transient GPU pressure from a neighbor job. This led to ~8 minute window where new requests were routed to hosted variants. Logged as INT-4421.

2026-03-13 16:12 - Support (Elsa Martinez): Shared preliminary findings with customer and proposed a partial invoice credit for hosted fallback charges while we perform permanent mitigations to autoscaler config. Asked customer if they accept a one-time credit and whether they want us to pull extended logs for reconciliation.

2026-03-14 09:01 - Customer (BrightLens - Taylor Ng): Requested a full refund for the $2,700, stating the job was scheduled with guaranteed capacity and they were not warned. Asked for mitigation so the incident does not recur.
root_cause: Autoscaler cooldown misconfiguration on dedicated pool 'dedic-pool-bltl-1' caused scale-down during a high-concurrency batch window. Router's fallback policy routed new requests to hosted runtime while dedicated pool was transiently under-provisioned. Billing correctly recorded execution on hosted instances; estimator does not currently account for short-duration fallback risk.
resolution: Proposed resolution: 1) Issue a goodwill credit for the full $2,700 pending customer acceptance. 2) Apply a corrective autoscaler configuration: increase scale-in cooldown and enable burst buffer headroom on dedicated pool 'dedic-pool-bltl-1'. 3) Create a Console notice explaining estimator limitations and add a 'fallback risk' indicator for large batch runs. 4) Reconcile invoice records and mark fallback usage as reviewed. Current status: credit pending customer confirmation; autoscaler config change staged in canary (PR #5472).
next_steps: 1) Wait for customer approval of $2,700 goodwill credit (Support to confirm). 2) SRE to deploy autoscaler cooldown fix to canaries and monitor for one week, link results back to this ticket. 3) Product to prioritize estimator enhancement to surface fallback-risk flag (tracked under internal backlog). 4) Finance to prepare credit memo draft for INV-2026-03-BL123 once customer approves. 5) Close loop with customer by 2026-03-18.
customer_request: Full reversal of the $2,700 hosted fallback charge and written assurance that the dedicated pool will not route to hosted by default for scheduled batch windows; specific request to add proactive estimator warnings for scheduled high-concurrency jobs.
